architecture_scope: Offline symbolic compilation and Python reference wrappers dispatching fixed existing native programs. No HIR, planner or executor modifications.

symbolic_scan.models: Independent X faults on every physical qubit before first T; independent Y faults on every physical qubit after last T. Not full circuit-level depolarizing noise.

fixed_frame_summary.interpretation: Exact common-Pauli-body representation size for the unmeasured preparation under one shared Clifford decoder and arbitrary Pauli signs. Not a sampling lower bound. Gate-target study allows X/Y faults after unitary targets and no noisy measurement/reset gadgets.

benchmarks.baseline: Current default HIR passes plus opt-in ActiveWidthSchedulePass
benchmarks.candidate: Same native compiler for resynthesized leaves; Python NumPy stochastic orchestration
benchmarks.timing_method: Five alternating repeats; per-arm shot budgets calibrated toward 0.15 seconds, with minimum 16 and maximum 1000000 shots. Median wall time per attempted shot; includes noise and postselection; excludes compilation and warmup. One thread and batch size one. Target is a calibration budget, not a hard timeout.

six_site_bank.scope: Exact independent-X models restricted to selected sites before first T. Branch bank fully enumerated and compiled up front. Timings include fault draws, grouping, dispatch and native sampling, but exclude compile and warmup.

affine_post_t.scope: Independent Pauli faults at every physical qubit at one selected layer, not throughout the circuit. One fixed native sampler plus precomputed affine record flips. Sampling includes noise draws, NumPy parity evaluation and postselection, and excludes compile and warmup.

affine_pre_t.scope: Independent Pauli faults at every physical qubit at one selected layer, not throughout the circuit. One fixed native sampler plus precomputed affine record flips. Sampling includes noise draws, NumPy parity evaluation and postselection, and excludes compile and warmup.

validation.reference_checks: Exact Aer full joint records and branch states for selected paths; stochastic Clifford models independently checked against Stim. Timing-run count agreement is an additional smoke check, with limited baseline shots on the most expensive cases.

limitations: Corpus inputs have no stochastic noise; benchmark models insert independent binary Pauli channels. These are not full depolarizing circuit noise benchmarks.
Trajectory algebra can be averaged with categorical Pauli probabilities, but the reference wrappers currently draw independent binary fault selectors only.
Prepared pure-state nullity staying one does not guarantee a single fixed native sampling plan with peak width one under arbitrary Pauli noise.
Branch banks grow exponentially with selected fault count and are not a production backend.
No new gains are established for current clifft-bench circuits outside this preparation fragment.
